profile.rtp_frame_shape: Video MediaFrame payload is a complete validated RTP packet. Native source sequence, marker and timestamp survive. Browser packets larger than the native bound are split preserving VP8 descriptor/body bytes, timestamp and final marker; bounded sequence translation retains loss gaps, maps exact duplicates consistently and drops unresolved late packets. Destination SSRC/PT are local. CSRC/extensions/padding are stripped.

architecture: Native-to-native uses explicit authorized UCTP subscriptions and core fanout; lifecycle-only pairing propagates peer termination without consuming source frame receivers.
Native-to-WebRTC and WebRTC-to-WebRTC use owned encoded-video forwarding beside the owned audio bridge.

WebRTC distinct authenticated participants are enabled for a current accepted AV Session selected by paired Conversation/Session IDs or the configured default, restricted to the configured participant pair; audio routes retain the configured-credential restriction.
Both leg authorities are checked at pairing and every second thereafter. Video owners cancel and join on peer termination and shutdown.
Connect explicitly supplies raw QUIC VP8 capability descriptor and default audio codecs plus VP8 subscriber accepted-codec policy; upstream audio-only defaults remain intact.
Native grants admit the exact PCMU plus VP8 duplex profile and reject duplicate IDs, additional cameras, unsupported codecs and one-way video.
Store binding atomically admits at most one current video connection per participant and permits idempotent binding/reconnect after unbind.
Browser video admission requires one active duplex VP8 video section plus one duplex audio section, no simulcast/RID, before peer allocation.

Authenticated PLI/FIR for an exact local WebRTC video SSRC is coalesced and normalized to an upstream PLI by a bridge-owned worker with at most four requests per second. Native UCTP has no feedback wire profile and relies on the approved at-most-one-second periodic keyframe interval.
Connect AV WebRTC peer creation registers only VP8; default upstream codec behavior remains unchanged. Generated real SDP regression verifies that VP9/H264 cannot be offered by the opt-in profile.

After acquiring the installation lock, startup atomically reconciles interrupted AV binding observations and emits session_interrupted while preserving a reconnectable accepted Session. Fresh physical connections require current authorization.

Explicit externally owned Core projections become idle on last transient detach; ordinary Core origin retains auto-end. Bounded origin/tombstone registry denies foreign/adopted/terminal revival, and durable terminal lookup releases idle projections without sockets.

Shutdown cancels in-progress owned media event preparation before binding cleanup, starts native endpoint drain immediately and joins independent WebRTC routes concurrently; genuine incomplete AV regression completes in 96-101 ms.
Connect current Store authority callback runs before PeerConnection or UDP allocation for selected and default AV offers; media ingress and lifecycle revalidate afterward.

Authenticated Health exposes bounded numeric process aggregates with sampled queue depths, exact dequeue-age boundary, histogram upper-bound forwarding percentiles and typed QUIC outcomes; no identity, credentials or media bytes.

QUIC VP8 egress adapts normalized RTP fragments to actual peer max_datagram_size minus the eight-byte UCTP header. Opt-in physical peer send buffer is 76032 shared audio/video bytes; opaque Quinn eviction and age remain unobserved.
